topics.label: Lecture opening and overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and outlines the scope of the lecture on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate immune recognition, pattern recognition receptors, and signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system detects microbes and tissue damage through molecular patterns, pattern recognition receptors, and downstream signaling complexes like the inflammasome.

topics.label: Inflammatory activation, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic complications
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the functional consequences of immune activation, covering sentinel cell mediator release, leukocyte extravasation, lymphatic priming, and severe systemic reactions like sepsis.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how acute inflammation is terminated, how tissue repair is coordinated, and how unresolved damage or persistent infection leads to chronic pathology and granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture closing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation and announces the topic of the following lecture.
